# Feature Requirements: Slugify String Utility

## Overview

A text transformation utility function that converts arbitrary strings into URL-safe, normalized slug formats. This utility is needed to support consistent identifier generation, URL-friendly text handling, and standardized string normalization across the project.

## Business Context

**Problem**: The application needs a standardized way to convert user-facing text (titles, names, labels) into machine-readable, URL-safe identifiers that are human-readable and consistent.

**Value**: Provides a reusable, predictable utility for generating slugs from arbitrary text input, ensuring consistency in identifier formatting across all system components.

## Functional Requirements

### REQ-001: Text Case Normalization
**Priority**: Must Have
**Actor**: Developer/System
**Description**: The utility must convert all input text to lowercase to ensure case-insensitive, consistent slug output.
**Rationale**: Lowercase normalization prevents duplicate identifiers that differ only in case and ensures predictable URL behavior.
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- All uppercase letters (A-Z) are converted to lowercase (a-z)
- Already lowercase text remains unchanged
- Mixed-case input produces lowercase output
- Example: "Hello World" → "hello world" (before other transformations)

### REQ-002: Whitespace and Underscore Replacement
**Priority**: Must Have
**Actor**: Developer/System
**Description**: The utility must replace all space characters and underscores with single hyphens.
**Rationale**: Hyphens are the standard word separator in URL slugs and improve readability while maintaining URL safety.
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Single space characters are replaced with a single hyphen
- Multiple consecutive spaces are collapsed to a single hyphen
- Underscore characters (_) are replaced with hyphens
- Multiple consecutive underscores are collapsed to a single hyphen
- Example: "Foo  Bar" → "foo-bar", "Foo__Bar" → "foo-bar"

### REQ-003: Character Filtering
**Priority**: Must Have
**Actor**: Developer/System
**Description**: The utility must remove any character that is not a letter (a-z), number (0-9), or hyphen (-).
**Rationale**: URL-safe slugs should contain only alphanumeric characters and hyphens, removing special characters, punctuation, and symbols that could cause encoding issues.
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Letters a-z are retained
- Numbers 0-9 are retained
- Hyphens (-) are retained
- All other characters (punctuation, special symbols, etc.) are removed
- Example: "Hello, World!" → "hello-world" (comma and exclamation removed)

### REQ-004: Hyphen Collapsing
**Priority**: Must Have
**Actor**: Developer/System
**Description**: The utility must collapse sequences of multiple consecutive hyphens into a single hyphen.
**Rationale**: Multiple hyphens reduce readability and create unnecessarily long slugs.
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Two or more consecutive hyphens are replaced with a single hyphen
- Single hyphens remain unchanged
- Example: "a---b" → "a-b", "foo--bar" → "foo-bar"

### REQ-005: Hyphen Trimming
**Priority**: Must Have
**Actor**: Developer/System
**Description**: The utility must remove leading and trailing hyphens from the output slug.
**Rationale**: Slugs should start and end with alphanumeric characters for consistency and to avoid edge cases in URL processing.
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Hyphens at the beginning of the slug are removed
- Hyphens at the end of the slug are removed
- Internal hyphens remain unchanged
- Example: "-hello-world-" → "hello-world"

### REQ-006: Function Interface
**Priority**: Must Have
**Actor**: Developer
**Description**: The utility must be exposed as a function named `slugify` that accepts a single text parameter and returns a string.
**Rationale**: Clear, standard function naming and interface enables easy discovery and usage by developers.
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Function is named `slugify`
- Function accepts one parameter: a string to be converted
- Function returns a string containing the slugified result
- Function is exported from the utils module for reuse

## User Stories

### STORY-001: Developer Uses Slugify for Title Conversion
**As a** developer implementing a feature
**I want** to convert user-provided titles into URL-safe slugs
**So that** I can generate consistent, readable URLs without manual string manipulation

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- GIVEN a user title "Hello, World!"
- WHEN I call `slugify("Hello, World!")`
- THEN I receive "hello-world"

### STORY-002: Developer Handles Text with Multiple Spaces
**As a** developer
**I want** the slugify function to normalize irregular spacing
**So that** inconsistent user input produces clean, uniform slugs

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- GIVEN text with multiple spaces "Foo  Bar"
- WHEN I call `slugify("Foo  Bar")`
- THEN I receive "foo-bar"

### STORY-003: Developer Converts Underscored Text
**As a** developer
**I want** underscores to be converted to hyphens
**So that** slugs follow URL conventions regardless of input format

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- GIVEN text with underscores "Foo__Bar"
- WHEN I call `slugify("Foo__Bar")`
- THEN I receive "foo-bar"

### STORY-004: Developer Normalizes Hyphenated Text
**As a** developer
**I want** excessive hyphens to be collapsed
**So that** slugs remain concise and readable

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- GIVEN text with repeated hyphens "a---b"
- WHEN I call `slugify("a---b")`
- THEN I receive "a-b"

## Test Cases

### TC-001: Basic Text with Punctuation
- **Input**: "Hello, World!"
- **Expected Output**: "hello-world"
- **Validates**: REQ-001, REQ-002, REQ-003

### TC-002: Multiple Spaces
- **Input**: "Foo  Bar"
- **Expected Output**: "foo-bar"
- **Validates**: REQ-002, REQ-004

### TC-003: Multiple Underscores
- **Input**: "Foo__Bar"
- **Expected Output**: "foo-bar"
- **Validates**: REQ-002, REQ-004

### TC-004: Repeated Hyphens
- **Input**: "a---b"
- **Expected Output**: "a-b"
- **Validates**: REQ-004

### TC-005: Leading and Trailing Hyphens
- **Input**: "-hello-world-"
- **Expected Output**: "hello-world"
- **Validates**: REQ-005

### TC-006: Mixed Case
- **Input**: "HeLLo WoRLd"
- **Expected Output**: "hello-world"
- **Validates**: REQ-001, REQ-002

### TC-007: Alphanumeric with Special Characters
- **Input**: "Test123!@#456"
- **Expected Output**: "test123456"
- **Validates**: REQ-001, REQ-003

### TC-008: Empty String
- **Input**: ""
- **Expected Output**: ""
- **Validates**: All requirements (edge case)

### TC-009: Only Special Characters
- **Input**: "!@#$%"
- **Expected Output**: ""
- **Validates**: REQ-003, REQ-005 (edge case)

### TC-010: Complex Real-World Example
- **Input**: "  Hello,  World!__Test---123  "
- **Expected Output**: "hello-world-test-123"
- **Validates**: All requirements combined

## Non-Functional Requirements

### NFR-001: Performance
**Category**: Performance
**Description**: The slugify function must execute efficiently for typical input strings (up to 1000 characters).
**Rationale**: String utilities are often called frequently and should not introduce performance bottlenecks.
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Function completes in under 10ms for strings up to 1000 characters
- No memory leaks or excessive allocations

### NFR-002: Reliability
**Category**: Reliability
**Description**: The function must handle all string inputs without errors, including edge cases like empty strings, Unicode characters, and very long strings.
**Rationale**: Defensive programming prevents runtime errors in production.
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Function never throws exceptions for any string input
- Function handles null/undefined gracefully (if applicable to language)
- Function handles Unicode characters appropriately (either preserve or remove consistently)

### NFR-003: Maintainability
**Category**: Maintainability
**Description**: The implementation must be clear, well-documented, and testable.
**Rationale**: Utility functions should be easy to understand and modify as requirements evolve.
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Function includes inline comments explaining transformation logic
- Function is covered by unit tests
- Function logic is broken into clear, sequential steps

## Success Metrics

- **Functional Completeness**: All test cases (TC-001 through TC-010) pass
- **Test Coverage**: 100% code coverage for the slugify function
- **Usage Adoption**: Function is used in at least one feature requiring slug generation

## Dependencies

None identified. This is a standalone utility function.

## Constraints

- Must be implemented in TypeScript (per project tech stack)
- Must be added to the existing `src/utils.ts` module
- Must follow existing project code patterns

# Technical Design: Slugify String Utility

## Overview

This design describes the implementation of a `slugify` utility function that transforms arbitrary strings into URL-safe, normalized slug formats. The function will be added to the existing `src/utils.ts` module following established project patterns.

## Architecture

### System Context

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph Application
        A[src/index.ts] --> B[src/utils.ts]
        C[Future Features] --> B
    end
    B --> D[slugify function]
```

The `slugify` function is a pure utility with no external dependencies. It integrates into the existing utils module and can be consumed by any module requiring slug generation.

### Component Design

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Input[Input String] --> Step1[1. Lowercase Conversion]
    Step1 --> Step2[2. Whitespace/Underscore Replacement]
    Step2 --> Step3[3. Character Filtering]
    Step3 --> Step4[4. Hyphen Collapsing]
    Step4 --> Step5[5. Hyphen Trimming]
    Step5 --> Output[Output Slug]
```

The function implements a five-step transformation pipeline:

| Step | Operation | Implementation |
|------|-----------|----------------|
| 1 | Lowercase conversion | `String.prototype.toLowerCase()` |
| 2 | Whitespace/underscore replacement | Regex: `/[\s_]+/g` -> `-` |
| 3 | Character filtering | Regex: `/[^a-z0-9-]/g` -> `` |
| 4 | Hyphen collapsing | Regex: `/-+/g` -> `-` |
| 5 | Hyphen trimming | Regex: `/^-+\|-+$/g` -> `` |

### Data Flow

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Caller
    participant slugify

    Caller->>slugify: "Hello, World!"
    Note over slugify: toLowerCase()
    Note over slugify: "hello, world!"
    Note over slugify: replace /[\s_]+/g
    Note over slugify: "hello,-world!"
    Note over slugify: replace /[^a-z0-9-]/g
    Note over slugify: "hello-world"
    Note over slugify: replace /-+/g
    Note over slugify: "hello-world"
    Note over slugify: trim hyphens
    slugify-->>Caller: "hello-world"
```

## Technical Specification

### Function Interface

```typescript
/**
 * Convert a string to a URL-safe slug.
 *
 * Transforms input by:
 * 1. Converting to lowercase
 * 2. Replacing spaces and underscores with hyphens
 * 3. Removing non-alphanumeric characters (except hyphens)
 * 4. Collapsing multiple consecutive hyphens
 * 5. Trimming leading and trailing hyphens
 *
 * @param text - The string to slugify
 * @returns A URL-safe slug string
 *
 * @example
 * slugify("Hello, World!") // "hello-world"
 * slugify("Foo  Bar")      // "foo-bar"
 * slugify("a---b")         // "a-b"
 */
export function slugify(text: string): string;
```

### Implementation Approach

The implementation uses a chain of string transformations:

```typescript
export function slugify(text: string): string {
  return text
    .toLowerCase()                    // REQ-001: Case normalization
    .replace(/[\s_]+/g, '-')          // REQ-002: Whitespace/underscore -> hyphen
    .replace(/[^a-z0-9-]/g, '')       // REQ-003: Remove invalid characters
    .replace(/-+/g, '-')              // REQ-004: Collapse multiple hyphens
    .replace(/^-+|-+$/g, '');         // REQ-005: Trim leading/trailing hyphens
}
```

### Edge Case Handling

| Input | Output | Rationale |
|-------|--------|-----------|
| Empty string `""` | `""` | Pass-through, no transformation needed |
| Only special chars `"!@#$%"` | `""` | All chars filtered, hyphens trimmed |
| Only whitespace `"   "` | `""` | Converted to hyphens, then trimmed |
| Unicode chars `"cafe"` | `"cafe"` | ASCII letters preserved |
| Unicode chars `"caf?"` | `"caf"` | Non-ASCII removed per REQ-003 |

### Type Safety

TypeScript enforces the string input type at compile time. Runtime null/undefined checks are unnecessary as:
1. TypeScript strict mode prevents null/undefined assignment to string
2. The function operates on primitive string operations that handle empty strings gracefully

## Integration Points

### Module Integration

| Integration | Source | Target | Type |
|-------------|--------|--------|------|
| Export | `src/utils.ts` | Consumers | Named export |
| Import | Consumer modules | `src/utils.ts` | ESM import |

Example usage:
```typescript
import { slugify } from "./utils";

const slug = slugify("Hello, World!"); // "hello-world"
```

## Testing Strategy

### Test Categories

| Category | Description | Coverage |
|----------|-------------|----------|
| Basic transformation | Standard inputs with punctuation, spaces | TC-001 |
| Whitespace handling | Multiple spaces, tabs | TC-002 |
| Underscore handling | Single and multiple underscores | TC-003 |
| Hyphen handling | Multiple hyphens, leading/trailing | TC-004, TC-005 |

|-----------|------------|-------|

# Design Decisions: Slugify String Utility

## Decision Log

### DEC-001: Implementation Approach - Method Chaining vs Procedural

**Context**: The slugify function requires multiple string transformations. Two approaches are viable: method chaining or step-by-step with intermediate variables.

**Options Considered**:

| Option | Pros | Cons |
|--------|------|------|
| A: Method chaining | Concise, readable, idiomatic JS/TS | Slightly harder to debug intermediate steps |
| B: Procedural steps | Easier debugging, explicit intermediate values | More verbose, more lines of code |

**Decision**: Option A - Method chaining

**Rationale**:
- Matches idiomatic TypeScript/JavaScript patterns
- The transformation is simple enough that intermediate debugging is unlikely needed
- Results in cleaner, more maintainable code
- Follows the principle of keeping utility functions concise

### DEC-002: Regex vs String Methods

**Context**: Character replacement can be done via regex or iterative string methods.

**Options Considered**:

| Option | Pros | Cons |
|--------|------|------|
| A: Regular expressions | Declarative, handles all patterns in one operation | Regex syntax can be opaque |
| B: String iteration | More explicit logic | Much more verbose, slower |
| C: String.split/join | Simple for basic cases | Cannot handle complex patterns |

**Decision**: Option A - Regular expressions

**Rationale**:
- Regex is the standard approach for string pattern matching in JavaScript
- Performance is excellent for the patterns needed
- Patterns are simple and well-documented
- Aligns with common slug implementations in the ecosystem

### DEC-003: Order of Transformations

**Context**: The transformation order affects correctness. Multiple valid orderings exist.

**Options Considered**:

| Order | Result |
|-------|--------|
| A: lower -> replace spaces -> filter -> collapse -> trim | Correct |
| B: replace spaces -> lower -> filter -> collapse -> trim | Correct |
| C: filter -> replace spaces -> lower -> collapse -> trim | Incorrect (uppercase removed before lowercasing) |

**Decision**: Order A - Lowercase first, then replacements, then filtering

**Rationale**:
- Lowercasing first ensures the character filter `[^a-z0-9-]` works correctly
- Space/underscore replacement before filtering ensures hyphens are created before non-alpha removal
- Collapsing after filtering handles hyphens created by adjacent special characters
- Trimming last ensures clean output regardless of intermediate state

### DEC-004: Null/Undefined Handling

**Context**: NFR-002 requires graceful handling of edge cases. TypeScript provides compile-time type safety, but runtime guards are optional.

**Options Considered**:

| Option | Pros | Cons |
|--------|------|------|
| A: No runtime guard | Cleaner code, TypeScript enforces | Throws if called from untyped JS |
| B: Runtime type check | Defensive, works from JS | Adds unnecessary code for TS consumers |
| C: Type assertion + guard | Best of both | Over-engineered for utility function |

**Decision**: Option A - No runtime guard

**Rationale**:
- Project uses TypeScript strict mode
- All consumption is from TypeScript code
- Adding guards for hypothetical JS consumers adds complexity
- If JS interop is needed later, guards can be added

### DEC-005: Test Structure

**Context**: Tests can be organized as individual test cases or grouped by category.

**Options Considered**:

| Option | Pros | Cons |
|--------|------|------|
| A: Individual tests per case | Clear mapping to requirements | Many small tests |
| B: Grouped by transformation type | Logical organization | Harder to trace to requirements |
| C: Single test with multiple assertions | Concise | Poor failure isolation |

**Decision**: Option A - Individual tests per case

**Rationale**:
- Directly maps to the 10 test cases in requirements
- Clear traceability from test to requirement
- Follows existing pattern in utils.test.ts
- Better failure messages when a specific case fails

### DEC-006: Documentation Level

**Context**: The function needs documentation. Options range from minimal to extensive.

**Options Considered**:

| Option | Pros | Cons |
|--------|------|------|
| A: JSDoc with examples | Clear usage, IDE support | Slightly more code |
| B: Minimal one-line comment | Concise | Less helpful |
| C: Separate markdown docs | Thorough | Over-engineered for utility |

**Decision**: Option A - JSDoc with examples

**Rationale**:
- Matches existing pattern in utils.ts (JSDoc above each function)
- Provides IDE hover documentation
- Examples show expected behavior at a glance
- No external documentation maintenance needed

    12→
    13→## Overview
    14→
    15→A text transformation utility function that converts arbitrary strings into URL-safe, normalized slug formats. This utility is needed to support consistent identifier generation, URL-friendly text handling, and standardized string normalization across the project.
    16→
    17→## Business Context
    18→
    19→**Problem**: The application needs a standardized way to convert user-facing text (titles, names, labels) into machine-readable, URL-safe identifiers that are human-readable and consistent.
    20→

    22→
    23→## Functional Requirements
    24→
    25→### REQ-001: Text Case Normalization
    26→**Priority**: Must Have
    27→**Actor**: Developer/System
    28→**Description**: The utility must convert all input text to lowercase to ensure case-insensitive, consistent slug output.
    29→**Rationale**: Lowercase normalization prevents duplicate identifiers that differ only in case and ensures predictable URL behavior.
    30→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    31→- All uppercase letters (A-Z) are converted to lowercase (a-z)
    32→- Already lowercase text remains unchanged
    33→- Mixed-case input produces lowercase output
    34→- Example: "Hello World" → "hello world" (before other transformations)
    35→
    36→### REQ-002: Whitespace and Underscore Replacement
    37→**Priority**: Must Have
    38→**Actor**: Developer/System
    39→**Description**: The utility must replace all space characters and underscores with single hyphens.
    40→**Rationale**: Hyphens are the standard word separator in URL slugs and improve readability while maintaining URL safety.
    41→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    42→- Single space characters are replaced with a single hyphen
    43→- Multiple consecutive spaces are collapsed to a single hyphen
    44→- Underscore characters (_) are replaced with hyphens
    45→- Multiple consecutive underscores are collapsed to a single hyphen
    46→- Example: "Foo  Bar" → "foo-bar", "Foo__Bar" → "foo-bar"
    47→
    48→### REQ-003: Character Filtering
    49→**Priority**: Must Have
    50→**Actor**: Developer/System
    51→**Description**: The utility must remove any character that is not a letter (a-z), number (0-9), or hyphen (-).
    52→**Rationale**: URL-safe slugs should contain only alphanumeric characters and hyphens, removing special characters, punctuation, and symbols that could cause encoding issues.
    53→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    54→- Letters a-z are retained
    55→- Numbers 0-9 are retained
    56→- Hyphens (-) are retained
    57→- All other characters (punctuation, special symbols, etc.) are removed
    58→- Example: "Hello, World!" → "hello-world" (comma and exclamation removed)
    59→

    61→**Priority**: Must Have
    62→**Actor**: Developer/System
    63→**Description**: The utility must collapse sequences of multiple consecutive hyphens into a single hyphen.
    64→**Rationale**: Multiple hyphens reduce readability and create unnecessarily long slugs.
    65→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    66→- Two or more consecutive hyphens are replaced with a single hyphen
    67→- Single hyphens remain unchanged
    68→- Example: "a---b" → "a-b", "foo--bar" → "foo-bar"
    69→

    71→**Priority**: Must Have
    72→**Actor**: Developer/System
    73→**Description**: The utility must remove leading and trailing hyphens from the output slug.
    74→**Rationale**: Slugs should start and end with alphanumeric characters for consistency and to avoid edge cases in URL processing.

    76→- Hyphens at the beginning of the slug are removed
    77→- Hyphens at the end of the slug are removed
    78→- Internal hyphens remain unchanged
    79→- Example: "-hello-world-" → "hello-world"
    80→
    81→### REQ-006: Function Interface
    82→**Priority**: Must Have
    83→**Actor**: Developer

   150→#### Exhausted-Retry Escalation {#s4-3-7}
   151→
   152→Escalate without marking parent `implementation` failed while recovery remains.
   153→

Skipping this strands the worktrees and leaves the run unable to make progress: integration requires the primary unit's reviewer to have succeeded, which will never happen for an escalated unit, so `schedule-wave` would keep reporting `pending_integration` forever.

    11→# Feature Requirements: Slugify String Utility
    12→
    13→## Overview
    14→
    15→A text transformation utility function that converts arbitrary strings into URL-safe, normalized slug formats. This utility is needed to support consistent identifier generation, URL-friendly text handling, and standardized string normalization across the project.
    16→
    17→## Business Context
    18→
    19→**Problem**: The application needs a standardized way to convert user-facing text (titles, names, labels) into machine-readable, URL-safe identifiers that are human-readable and consistent.
    20→
    21→**Value**: Provides a reusable, predictable utility for generating slugs from arbitrary text input, ensuring consistency in identifier formatting across all system components.
    22→
    23→## Functional Requirements
    24→
    25→### REQ-001: Text Case Normalization
    26→**Priority**: Must Have
    27→**Actor**: Developer/System
    28→**Description**: The utility must convert all input text to lowercase to ensure case-insensitive, consistent slug output.
    29→**Rationale**: Lowercase normalization prevents duplicate identifiers that differ only in case and ensures predictable URL behavior.
    30→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    31→- All uppercase letters (A-Z) are converted to lowercase (a-z)
    32→- Already lowercase text remains unchanged
    33→- Mixed-case input produces lowercase output
    34→- Example: "Hello World" → "hello world" (before other transformations)
    35→
    36→### REQ-002: Whitespace and Underscore Replacement
    37→**Priority**: Must Have
    38→**Actor**: Developer/System
    39→**Description**: The utility must replace all space characters and underscores with single hyphens.
    40→**Rationale**: Hyphens are the standard word separator in URL slugs and improve readability while maintaining URL safety.
    41→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    42→- Single space characters are replaced with a single hyphen
    43→- Multiple consecutive spaces are collapsed to a single hyphen
    44→- Underscore characters (_) are replaced with hyphens
    45→- Multiple consecutive underscores are collapsed to a single hyphen
    46→- Example: "Foo  Bar" → "foo-bar", "Foo__Bar" → "foo-bar"
    47→
    48→### REQ-003: Character Filtering
    49→**Priority**: Must Have
    50→**Actor**: Developer/System
    51→**Description**: The utility must remove any character that is not a letter (a-z), number (0-9), or hyphen (-).
    52→**Rationale**: URL-safe slugs should contain only alphanumeric characters and hyphens, removing special characters, punctuation, and symbols that could cause encoding issues.
    53→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    54→- Letters a-z are retained
    55→- Numbers 0-9 are retained
    56→- Hyphens (-) are retained
    57→- All other characters (punctuation, special symbols, etc.) are removed
    58→- Example: "Hello, World!" → "hello-world" (comma and exclamation removed)
    59→
    60→### REQ-004: Hyphen Collapsing
    61→**Priority**: Must Have
    62→**Actor**: Developer/System
    63→**Description**: The utility must collapse sequences of multiple consecutive hyphens into a single hyphen.
    64→**Rationale**: Multiple hyphens reduce readability and create unnecessarily long slugs.
    65→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    66→- Two or more consecutive hyphens are replaced with a single hyphen
    67→- Single hyphens remain unchanged
    68→- Example: "a---b" → "a-b", "foo--bar" → "foo-bar"
    69→
    70→### REQ-005: Hyphen Trimming
    71→**Priority**: Must Have
    72→**Actor**: Developer/System
    73→**Description**: The utility must remove leading and trailing hyphens from the output slug.
    74→**Rationale**: Slugs should start and end with alphanumeric characters for consistency and to avoid edge cases in URL processing.
    75→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    76→- Hyphens at the beginning of the slug are removed
    77→- Hyphens at the end of the slug are removed
    78→- Internal hyphens remain unchanged
    79→- Example: "-hello-world-" → "hello-world"
    80→
    81→### REQ-006: Function Interface
    82→**Priority**: Must Have
    83→**Actor**: Developer
    84→**Description**: The utility must be exposed as a function named `slugify` that accepts a single text parameter and returns a string.
    85→**Rationale**: Clear, standard function naming and interface enables easy discovery and usage by developers.
    86→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    87→- Function is named `slugify`
    88→- Function accepts one parameter: a string to be converted
    89→- Function returns a string containing the slugified result
    90→- Function is exported from the utils module for reuse
    91→
    92→## User Stories
    93→
    94→### STORY-001: Developer Uses Slugify for Title Conversion
    95→**As a** developer implementing a feature
    96→**I want** to convert user-provided titles into URL-safe slugs
    97→**So that** I can generate consistent, readable URLs without manual string manipulation
    98→
    99→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   100→- GIVEN a user title "Hello, World!"
   101→- WHEN I call `slugify("Hello, World!")`
   102→- THEN I receive "hello-world"
   103→
   104→### STORY-002: Developer Handles Text with Multiple Spaces
   105→**As a** developer
   106→**I want** the slugify function to normalize irregular spacing
   107→**So that** inconsistent user input produces clean, uniform slugs
   108→
   109→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   110→- GIVEN text with multiple spaces "Foo  Bar"
   111→- WHEN I call `slugify("Foo  Bar")`
   112→- THEN I receive "foo-bar"
   113→
   114→### STORY-003: Developer Converts Underscored Text
   115→**As a** developer
   116→**I want** underscores to be converted to hyphens
   117→**So that** slugs follow URL conventions regardless of input format
   118→
   119→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   120→- GIVEN text with underscores "Foo__Bar"
   121→- WHEN I call `slugify("Foo__Bar")`
   122→- THEN I receive "foo-bar"
   123→
   124→### STORY-004: Developer Normalizes Hyphenated Text
   125→**As a** developer
   126→**I want** excessive hyphens to be collapsed
   127→**So that** slugs remain concise and readable
   128→
   129→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   130→- GIVEN text with repeated hyphens "a---b"
   131→- WHEN I call `slugify("a---b")`
   132→- THEN I receive "a-b"
   133→
   134→## Test Cases
   135→
   136→### TC-001: Basic Text with Punctuation
   137→- **Input**: "Hello, World!"
   138→- **Expected Output**: "hello-world"
   139→- **Validates**: REQ-001, REQ-002, REQ-003
   140→
   141→### TC-002: Multiple Spaces
   142→- **Input**: "Foo  Bar"
   143→- **Expected Output**: "foo-bar"
   144→- **Validates**: REQ-002, REQ-004
   145→
   146→### TC-003: Multiple Underscores
   147→- **Input**: "Foo__Bar"
   148→- **Expected Output**: "foo-bar"
   149→- **Validates**: REQ-002, REQ-004
   150→
   151→### TC-004: Repeated Hyphens
   152→- **Input**: "a---b"
   153→- **Expected Output**: "a-b"
   154→- **Validates**: REQ-004
   155→
   156→### TC-005: Leading and Trailing Hyphens
   157→- **Input**: "-hello-world-"
   158→- **Expected Output**: "hello-world"
   159→- **Validates**: REQ-005
   160→
   161→### TC-006: Mixed Case
   162→- **Input**: "HeLLo WoRLd"
   163→- **Expected Output**: "hello-world"
   164→- **Validates**: REQ-001, REQ-002
   165→
   166→### TC-007: Alphanumeric with Special Characters
   167→- **Input**: "Test123!@#456"
   168→- **Expected Output**: "test123456"
   169→- **Validates**: REQ-001, REQ-003
   170→
   171→### TC-008: Empty String
   172→- **Input**: ""
   173→- **Expected Output**: ""
   174→- **Validates**: All requirements (edge case)
   175→
   176→### TC-009: Only Special Characters
   177→- **Input**: "!@#$%"
   178→- **Expected Output**: ""
   179→- **Validates**: REQ-003, REQ-005 (edge case)
   180→
   181→### TC-010: Complex Real-World Example
   182→- **Input**: "  Hello,  World!__Test---123  "
   183→- **Expected Output**: "hello-world-test-123"
   184→- **Validates**: All requirements combined
   185→
   186→## Non-Functional Requirements
   187→
   188→### NFR-001: Performance
   189→**Category**: Performance
   190→**Description**: The slugify function must execute efficiently for typical input strings (up to 1000 characters).
   191→**Rationale**: String utilities are often called frequently and should not introduce performance bottlenecks.
   192→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   193→- Function completes in under 10ms for strings up to 1000 characters
   194→- No memory leaks or excessive allocations
   195→
   196→### NFR-002: Reliability
   197→**Category**: Reliability
   198→**Description**: The function must handle all string inputs without errors, including edge cases like empty strings, Unicode characters, and very long strings.
   199→**Rationale**: Defensive programming prevents runtime errors in production.
   200→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   201→- Function never throws exceptions for any string input
   202→- Function handles null/undefined gracefully (if applicable to language)
   203→- Function handles Unicode characters appropriately (either preserve or remove consistently)
   204→
   205→### NFR-003: Maintainability
   206→**Category**: Maintainability
   207→**Description**: The implementation must be clear, well-documented, and testable.
   208→**Rationale**: Utility functions should be easy to understand and modify as requirements evolve.
   209→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   210→- Function includes inline comments explaining transformation logic
   211→- Function is covered by unit tests
   212→- Function logic is broken into clear, sequential steps
   213→
   214→## Success Metrics
   215→
   216→- **Functional Completeness**: All test cases (TC-001 through TC-010) pass
   217→- **Test Coverage**: 100% code coverage for the slugify function
   218→- **Usage Adoption**: Function is used in at least one feature requiring slug generation
   219→
   220→## Dependencies
   221→
   222→None identified. This is a standalone utility function.
   223→
   224→## Constraints
   225→
   226→- Must be implemented in TypeScript (per project tech stack)
   227→- Must be added to the existing `src/utils.ts` module
   228→- Must follow existing project code patterns
   229→
   230→## Out of Scope
   231→
   232→- Internationalization (Unicode transliteration, e.g., converting "café" to "cafe")
   233→- Custom separator characters (only hyphens are supported)
   234→- Maximum length truncation
   235→- Uniqueness guarantees (responsibility of caller)
   236→- Slug validation or parsing (inverse operation)
   237→
   238→## AFK Mode Decisions
   239→
   240→This requirements document was generated in AFK (autonomous) mode. The following decisions were made automatically:
   241→
   242→### Decision 1: No PRD Association
   243→**Point**: PRD selection
   244→**Choice**: No parent PRD
   245→**Rationale**: No PRDs exist in `.rp1/work/prds/`. This is a standalone utility feature.
   246→
   247→### Decision 2: Standard String Handling
   248→**Point**: String edge cases
   249→**Choice**: Empty input returns empty output; only ASCII letters/numbers preserved
   250→**Rationale**: Conservative default behavior aligned with URL slug standards and the provided examples.
   251→
   252→### Decision 3: No Unicode Transliteration
   253→**Point**: Non-ASCII character handling
   254→**Choice**: Remove non-ASCII characters (letters outside a-z)
   255→**Rationale**: The requirement specifies "letter, number, or hyphen" without mentioning Unicode support. Conservative interpretation removes characters outside ASCII alphanumeric range.
   256→
   257→### Decision 4: Function Placement
   258→**Point**: Module location
   259→**Choice**: Add to existing `src/utils.ts` module
   260→**Rationale**: Knowledge base indicates `src/utils.ts` is the designated location for utility functions.
   261→
   262→### Decision 5: Null/Undefined Handling
   263→**Point**: Invalid input handling
   264→**Choice**: Treat as edge case for implementation to decide (document but don't mandate specific behavior)
   265→**Rationale**: TypeScript typing will likely prevent null/undefined, but NFR-002 requires graceful handling if applicable.
   266→
   267→## Notes
   268→
   269→- This utility follows common slug generation patterns used in CMS systems and URL routing libraries
   270→- The transformation order matters: case normalization → replacement → filtering → collapsing → trimming
   271→- Consider adding Unicode support (e.g., transliterating accented characters) in future iterations if needed

    10→
    11→# Technical Design: Slugify String Utility
    12→
    13→## Overview
    14→
    15→This design describes the implementation of a `slugify` utility function that transforms arbitrary strings into URL-safe, normalized slug formats. The function will be added to the existing `src/utils.ts` module following established project patterns.
    16→
    17→## Architecture
    18→
    19→### System Context
    20→
    21→```mermaid
    22→flowchart LR
    23→    subgraph Application
    24→        A[src/index.ts] --> B[src/utils.ts]
    25→        C[Future Features] --> B
    26→    end
    27→    B --> D[slugify function]
    28→```
    29→
    30→The `slugify` function is a pure utility with no external dependencies. It integrates into the existing utils module and can be consumed by any module requiring slug generation.
    31→
    32→### Component Design
    33→
    34→```mermaid
    35→flowchart TD
    36→    Input[Input String] --> Step1[1. Lowercase Conversion]
    37→    Step1 --> Step2[2. Whitespace/Underscore Replacement]
    38→    Step2 --> Step3[3. Character Filtering]
    39→    Step3 --> Step4[4. Hyphen Collapsing]
    40→    Step4 --> Step5[5. Hyphen Trimming]
    41→    Step5 --> Output[Output Slug]
    42→```
    43→
    44→The function implements a five-step transformation pipeline:
    45→
    46→| Step | Operation | Implementation |
    47→|------|-----------|----------------|
    48→| 1 | Lowercase conversion | `String.prototype.toLowerCase()` |
    49→| 2 | Whitespace/underscore replacement | Regex: `/[\s_]+/g` -> `-` |
    50→| 3 | Character filtering | Regex: `/[^a-z0-9-]/g` -> `` |
    51→| 4 | Hyphen collapsing | Regex: `/-+/g` -> `-` |
    52→| 5 | Hyphen trimming | Regex: `/^-+\|-+$/g` -> `` |
    53→
    54→### Data Flow
    55→
    56→```mermaid
    57→sequenceDiagram
    58→    participant Caller
    59→    participant slugify
    60→
    61→    Caller->>slugify: "Hello, World!"
    62→    Note over slugify: toLowerCase()
    63→    Note over slugify: "hello, world!"
    64→    Note over slugify: replace /[\s_]+/g
    65→    Note over slugify: "hello,-world!"
    66→    Note over slugify: replace /[^a-z0-9-]/g
    67→    Note over slugify: "hello-world"
    68→    Note over slugify: replace /-+/g
    69→    Note over slugify: "hello-world"
    70→    Note over slugify: trim hyphens
    71→    slugify-->>Caller: "hello-world"
    72→```
    73→
    74→## Technical Specification
    75→
    76→### Function Interface
    77→
    78→```typescript
    79→/**
    80→ * Convert a string to a URL-safe slug.
    81→ *
    82→ * Transforms input by:
    83→ * 1. Converting to lowercase
    84→ * 2. Replacing spaces and underscores with hyphens
    85→ * 3. Removing non-alphanumeric characters (except hyphens)
    86→ * 4. Collapsing multiple consecutive hyphens
    87→ * 5. Trimming leading and trailing hyphens
    88→ *
    89→ * @param text - The string to slugify
    90→ * @returns A URL-safe slug string
    91→ *
    92→ * @example
    93→ * slugify("Hello, World!") // "hello-world"
    94→ * slugify("Foo  Bar")      // "foo-bar"
    95→ * slugify("a---b")         // "a-b"
    96→ */
    97→export function slugify(text: string): string;
    98→```
    99→
   100→### Implementation Approach
   101→
   102→The implementation uses a chain of string transformations:
   103→
   104→```typescript
   105→export function slugify(text: string): string {
   106→  return text
   107→    .toLowerCase()                    // REQ-001: Case normalization
   108→    .replace(/[\s_]+/g, '-')          // REQ-002: Whitespace/underscore -> hyphen
   109→    .replace(/[^a-z0-9-]/g, '')       // REQ-003: Remove invalid characters
   110→    .replace(/-+/g, '-')              // REQ-004: Collapse multiple hyphens
   111→    .replace(/^-+|-+$/g, '');         // REQ-005: Trim leading/trailing hyphens
   112→}
   113→```
   114→
   115→### Edge Case Handling
   116→
   117→| Input | Output | Rationale |
   118→|-------|--------|-----------|
   119→| Empty string `""` | `""` | Pass-through, no transformation needed |
   120→| Only special chars `"!@#$%"` | `""` | All chars filtered, hyphens trimmed |
   121→| Only whitespace `"   "` | `""` | Converted to hyphens, then trimmed |
   122→| Unicode chars `"cafe"` | `"cafe"` | ASCII letters preserved |
   123→| Unicode chars `"caf?"` | `"caf"` | Non-ASCII removed per REQ-003 |
   124→
   125→### Type Safety
   126→
   127→TypeScript enforces the string input type at compile time. Runtime null/undefined checks are unnecessary as:
   128→1. TypeScript strict mode prevents null/undefined assignment to string
   129→2. The function operates on primitive string operations that handle empty strings gracefully
   130→
   131→## Integration Points
   132→
   133→### Module Integration
   134→
   135→| Integration | Source | Target | Type |
   136→|-------------|--------|--------|------|
   137→| Export | `src/utils.ts` | Consumers | Named export |
   138→| Import | Consumer modules | `src/utils.ts` | ESM import |
   139→
   140→Example usage:
   141→```typescript
   142→import { slugify } from "./utils";
   143→
   144→const slug = slugify("Hello, World!"); // "hello-world"
   145→```
   146→
   147→## Testing Strategy
   148→
   149→### Test Categories
   150→
   151→| Category | Description | Coverage |
   152→|----------|-------------|----------|
   153→| Basic transformation | Standard inputs with punctuation, spaces | TC-001 |
   154→| Whitespace handling | Multiple spaces, tabs | TC-002 |
   155→| Underscore handling | Single and multiple underscores | TC-003 |
   156→| Hyphen handling | Multiple hyphens, leading/trailing | TC-004, TC-005 |
   157→| Case normalization | Mixed case inputs | TC-006 |
   158→| Character filtering | Special characters, symbols | TC-007 |
   159→| Edge cases | Empty string, only special chars | TC-008, TC-009 |
   160→| Complex inputs | Combined transformations | TC-010 |
   161→
   162→### Test Implementation
   163→
   164→Tests will be added to `src/utils.test.ts` following the existing pattern:
   165→
   166→```typescript
   167→describe("slugify", () => {
   168→  test("converts text with punctuation to slug", () => {
   169→    expect(slugify("Hello, World!")).toBe("hello-world");
   170→  });
   171→
   172→  test("collapses multiple spaces", () => {
   173→    expect(slugify("Foo  Bar")).toBe("foo-bar");
   174→  });
   175→
   176→  // ... additional test cases
   177→});
   178→```
   179→
   180→### Coverage Requirements
   181→
   182→- All 10 test cases from requirements must pass
   183→- Each requirement (REQ-001 through REQ-006) must have at least one test
   184→- Edge cases (empty string, only special chars) must be covered
   185→
   186→## Performance Considerations
   187→
   188→### Complexity Analysis
   189→
   190→| Operation | Complexity | Notes |
   191→|-----------|------------|-------|
   192→| toLowerCase | O(n) | Single pass |
   193→| Each regex replace | O(n) | Single pass per regex |
   194→| Total | O(n) | Linear in input length |
   195→
   196→### Benchmarks
   197→
   198→For typical inputs (< 1000 characters), expected execution time is < 1ms. The regex engine is highly optimized for these simple patterns.
   199→
   200→### Memory
   201→
   202→- No intermediate allocations beyond string results
   203→- Chained method calls create temporary strings (expected JavaScript behavior)
   204→- No memory leaks possible (pure function, no retained references)
   205→
   206→## Error Handling
   207→
   208→The function is designed to never throw exceptions:
   209→
   210→| Scenario | Behavior |
   211→|----------|----------|
   212→| Empty string | Returns empty string |
   213→| Null/undefined | TypeScript prevents; if bypassed, `.toLowerCase()` would throw |
   214→| Very long string | Processes linearly; JavaScript string limit is ~512MB |
   215→
   216→For defensive runtime handling (if needed for JavaScript consumers), a guard could be added:
   217→```typescript
   218→if (typeof text !== 'string') return '';
   219→```
   220→
   221→This is **not recommended** for the initial implementation as TypeScript provides compile-time guarantees.
   222→
   223→## Implementation Plan
   224→
   225→### Task Breakdown
   226→
   227→| Task | Description | Estimate |
   228→|------|-------------|----------|
   229→| T1 | Implement `slugify` function in `src/utils.ts` | 10 min |
   230→| T2 | Add test cases to `src/utils.test.ts` | 15 min |
   231→
   232→### Implementation DAG
   233→
   234→**Parallel Groups** (tasks with no inter-dependencies):
   235→
   236→1. [T1, T2] - Function and tests can be written in parallel since interface is defined
   237→
   238→**Dependencies**:
   239→
   240→- T2 verification -> T1 (tests verify implementation correctness)
   241→
   242→**Critical Path**: T1 -> T2
   243→
   244→### Verification Steps
   245→
   246→1. Run `bun test` to execute all tests
   247→2. Verify all 10 test cases pass
   248→3. Confirm no regressions in existing `greet` and `add` tests
   249→
   250→## Documentation Impact
   251→
   252→| Type | Target | Section | KB Source | Rationale |
   253→|------|--------|---------|-----------|-----------|
   254→| Code | `src/utils.ts` | JSDoc | patterns.md | Document function purpose and examples |
   255→| None | - | - | - | No external documentation required |
   256→
   257→## Security Considerations
   258→
   259→- **Input validation**: Function accepts any string; no injection risk as output is sanitized
   260→- **Output safety**: Resulting slugs contain only `[a-z0-9-]`, safe for URLs
   261→- **No external calls**: Pure function with no network or filesystem access
   262→
   263→## Future Considerations
   264→
   265→The following enhancements are explicitly out of scope but may be considered later:
   266→
   267→1. **Unicode transliteration**: Convert accented characters (e.g., "caf?" -> "cafe")
   268→2. **Custom separators**: Allow configuring separator character
   269→3. **Length truncation**: Limit slug length with word-boundary awareness
   270→4. **Uniqueness**: Generate unique slugs by appending counters
   271→
   272→These would require additional requirements and design work.
   273→

/**
 * Add two numbers.
 */
export function add(a: number, b: number): number {
  return a + b;
}

/**
 * Convert a string to a URL-safe slug.
 *
 * Transforms input by:
 * 1. Converting to lowercase
 * 2. Replacing spaces and underscores with hyphens
 * 3. Removing non-alphanumeric characters (except hyphens)
 * 4. Collapsing multiple consecutive hyphens
 * 5. Trimming leading and trailing hyphens
 *
 * @param text - The string to slugify
 * @returns A URL-safe slug string
 *
 * @example
 * slugify("Hello, World!") // "hello-world"
 * slugify("Foo  Bar")      // "foo-bar"
 * slugify("a---b")         // "a-b"
 */
export function slugify(text: string): string {
  return text
    .toLowerCase()
    .replace(/[\s_]+/g, '-')
    .replace(/[^a-z0-9-]/g, '')
    .replace(/-+/g, '-')
    .replace(/^-+|-+$/g, '');
}

    52→| 5 | Hyphen trimming | Regex: `/^-+\|-+$/g` -> `` |
    53→
    54→### Data Flow
    55→
    56→```mermaid
    57→sequenceDiagram
    58→    participant Caller
    59→    participant slugify
    60→
    61→    Caller->>slugify: "Hello, World!"
    62→    Note over slugify: toLowerCase()
    63→    Note over slugify: "hello, world!"
    64→    Note over slugify: replace /[\s_]+/g
    65→    Note over slugify: "hello,-world!"
    66→    Note over slugify: replace /[^a-z0-9-]/g
    67→    Note over slugify: "hello-world"
    68→    Note over slugify: replace /-+/g
    69→    Note over slugify: "hello-world"
    70→    Note over slugify: trim hyphens
    71→    slugify-->>Caller: "hello-world"
    72→```
    73→
    74→## Technical Specification
    75→
    76→### Function Interface
    77→
    78→```typescript
    79→/**
    80→ * Convert a string to a URL-safe slug.
    81→ *
    82→ * Transforms input by:
    83→ * 1. Converting to lowercase
    84→ * 2. Replacing spaces and underscores with hyphens
    85→ * 3. Removing non-alphanumeric characters (except hyphens)
    86→ * 4. Collapsing multiple consecutive hyphens
    87→ * 5. Trimming leading and trailing hyphens
    88→ *
    89→ * @param text - The string to slugify
    90→ * @returns A URL-safe slug string
    91→ *
    92→ * @example
    93→ * slugify("Hello, World!") // "hello-world"
    94→ * slugify("Foo  Bar")      // "foo-bar"
    95→ * slugify("a---b")         // "a-b"
    96→ */
    97→export function slugify(text: string): string;
    98→```
    99→
   100→### Implementation Approach
   101→
   102→The implementation uses a chain of string transformations:
   103→
   104→```typescript
   105→export function slugify(text: string): string {
   106→  return text
   107→    .toLowerCase()                    // REQ-001: Case normalization
   108→    .replace(/[\s_]+/g, '-')          // REQ-002: Whitespace/underscore -> hyphen
   109→    .replace(/[^a-z0-9-]/g, '')       // REQ-003: Remove invalid characters
   110→    .replace(/-+/g, '-')              // REQ-004: Collapse multiple hyphens
   111→    .replace(/^-+|-+$/g, '');         // REQ-005: Trim leading/trailing hyphens
   112→}
   113→```
   114→
   115→### Edge Case Handling
   116→
   117→| Input | Output | Rationale |
   118→|-------|--------|-----------|
   119→| Empty string `""` | `""` | Pass-through, no transformation needed |
   120→| Only special chars `"!@#$%"` | `""` | All chars filtered, hyphens trimmed |
   121→| Only whitespace `"   "` | `""` | Converted to hyphens, then trimmed |
   122→| Unicode chars `"cafe"` | `"cafe"` | ASCII letters preserved |
   123→| Unicode chars `"caf?"` | `"caf"` | Non-ASCII removed per REQ-003 |
   124→
   125→### Type Safety
   126→
   127→TypeScript enforces the string input type at compile time. Runtime null/undefined checks are unnecessary as:
   128→1. TypeScript strict mode prevents null/undefined assignment to string
   129→2. The function operates on primitive string operations that handle empty strings gracefully
   130→
   131→## Integration Points
   132→
   133→### Module Integration
   134→
   135→| Integration | Source | Target | Type |
   136→|-------------|--------|--------|------|
   137→| Export | `src/utils.ts` | Consumers | Named export |
   138→| Import | Consumer modules | `src/utils.ts` | ESM import |
   139→
   140→Example usage:
   141→```typescript
   142→import { slugify } from "./utils";
   143→
   144→const slug = slugify("Hello, World!"); // "hello-world"
   145→```
   146→
   147→## Testing Strategy
   148→
   149→### Test Categories
   150→
   151→| Category | Description | Coverage |
   152→|----------|-------------|----------|
   153→| Basic transformation | Standard inputs with punctuation, spaces | TC-001 |
   154→| Whitespace handling | Multiple spaces, tabs | TC-002 |
   155→| Underscore handling | Single and multiple underscores | TC-003 |
   156→| Hyphen handling | Multiple hyphens, leading/trailing | TC-004, TC-005 |
   157→| Case normalization | Mixed case inputs | TC-006 |
   158→| Character filtering | Special characters, symbols | TC-007 |
   159→| Edge cases | Empty string, only special chars | TC-008, TC-009 |
   160→| Complex inputs | Combined transformations | TC-010 |
   161→
   162→### Test Implementation
   163→
   164→Tests will be added to `src/utils.test.ts` following the existing pattern:
   165→
   166→```typescript
   167→describe("slugify", () => {
   168→  test("converts text with punctuation to slug", () => {
   169→    expect(slugify("Hello, World!")).toBe("hello-world");
   170→  });
   171→
   172→  test("collapses multiple spaces", () => {
   173→    expect(slugify("Foo  Bar")).toBe("foo-bar");
   174→  });
   175→
   176→  // ... additional test cases
   177→});
   178→```
   179→
   180→### Coverage Requirements
   181→
   182→- All 10 test cases from requirements must pass
   183→- Each requirement (REQ-001 through REQ-006) must have at least one test
   184→- Edge cases (empty string, only special chars) must be covered
   185→
   186→## Performance Considerations
   187→
   188→### Complexity Analysis
   189→
   190→| Operation | Complexity | Notes |
   191→|-----------|------------|-------|
   192→| toLowerCase | O(n) | Single pass |
   193→| Each regex replace | O(n) | Single pass per regex |
   194→| Total | O(n) | Linear in input length |
   195→
   196→### Benchmarks
   197→
   198→For typical inputs (< 1000 characters), expected execution time is < 1ms. The regex engine is highly optimized for these simple patterns.
   199→
   200→### Memory
   201→
   202→- No intermediate allocations beyond string results
   203→- Chained method calls create temporary strings (expected JavaScript behavior)
   204→- No memory leaks possible (pure function, no retained references)
   205→
   206→## Error Handling
   207→
   208→The function is designed to never throw exceptions:
   209→
   210→| Scenario | Behavior |
   211→|----------|----------|
   212→| Empty string | Returns empty string |
   213→| Null/undefined | TypeScript prevents; if bypassed, `.toLowerCase()` would throw |
   214→| Very long string | Processes linearly; JavaScript string limit is ~512MB |
   215→
   216→For defensive runtime handling (if needed for JavaScript consumers), a guard could be added:
   217→```typescript
   218→if (typeof text !== 'string') return '';
   219→```
   220→
   221→This is **not recommended** for the initial implementation as TypeScript provides compile-time guarantees.
   222→

   228→|------|-------------|----------|

   256→
   257→## Security Considerations
   258→
   259→- **Input validation**: Function accepts any string; no injection risk as output is sanitized
   260→- **Output safety**: Resulting slugs contain only `[a-z0-9-]`, safe for URLs
   261→- **No external calls**: Pure function with no network or filesystem access

    10→
    11→# Feature Requirements: Slugify String Utility
    12→
    13→## Overview
    14→
    15→A text transformation utility function that converts arbitrary strings into URL-safe, normalized slug formats. This utility is needed to support consistent identifier generation, URL-friendly text handling, and standardized string normalization across the project.
    16→
    17→## Business Context
    18→
    19→**Problem**: The application needs a standardized way to convert user-facing text (titles, names, labels) into machine-readable, URL-safe identifiers that are human-readable and consistent.
    20→
    21→**Value**: Provides a reusable, predictable utility for generating slugs from arbitrary text input, ensuring consistency in identifier formatting across all system components.
    22→
    23→## Functional Requirements
    24→
    25→### REQ-001: Text Case Normalization
    26→**Priority**: Must Have
    27→**Actor**: Developer/System
    28→**Description**: The utility must convert all input text to lowercase to ensure case-insensitive, consistent slug output.
    29→**Rationale**: Lowercase normalization prevents duplicate identifiers that differ only in case and ensures predictable URL behavior.
    30→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    31→- All uppercase letters (A-Z) are converted to lowercase (a-z)
    32→- Already lowercase text remains unchanged
    33→- Mixed-case input produces lowercase output
    34→- Example: "Hello World" → "hello world" (before other transformations)
    35→
    36→### REQ-002: Whitespace and Underscore Replacement
    37→**Priority**: Must Have
    38→**Actor**: Developer/System
    39→**Description**: The utility must replace all space characters and underscores with single hyphens.
    40→**Rationale**: Hyphens are the standard word separator in URL slugs and improve readability while maintaining URL safety.
    41→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    42→- Single space characters are replaced with a single hyphen
    43→- Multiple consecutive spaces are collapsed to a single hyphen
    44→- Underscore characters (_) are replaced with hyphens
    45→- Multiple consecutive underscores are collapsed to a single hyphen
    46→- Example: "Foo  Bar" → "foo-bar", "Foo__Bar" → "foo-bar"
    47→
    48→### REQ-003: Character Filtering
    49→**Priority**: Must Have
    50→**Actor**: Developer/System
    51→**Description**: The utility must remove any character that is not a letter (a-z), number (0-9), or hyphen (-).
    52→**Rationale**: URL-safe slugs should contain only alphanumeric characters and hyphens, removing special characters, punctuation, and symbols that could cause encoding issues.
    53→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    54→- Letters a-z are retained
    55→- Numbers 0-9 are retained
    56→- Hyphens (-) are retained
    57→- All other characters (punctuation, special symbols, etc.) are removed
    58→- Example: "Hello, World!" → "hello-world" (comma and exclamation removed)
    59→
    60→### REQ-004: Hyphen Collapsing
    61→**Priority**: Must Have
    62→**Actor**: Developer/System
    63→**Description**: The utility must collapse sequences of multiple consecutive hyphens into a single hyphen.
    64→**Rationale**: Multiple hyphens reduce readability and create unnecessarily long slugs.
    65→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    66→- Two or more consecutive hyphens are replaced with a single hyphen
    67→- Single hyphens remain unchanged
    68→- Example: "a---b" → "a-b", "foo--bar" → "foo-bar"
    69→
    70→### REQ-005: Hyphen Trimming
    71→**Priority**: Must Have
    72→**Actor**: Developer/System
    73→**Description**: The utility must remove leading and trailing hyphens from the output slug.
    74→**Rationale**: Slugs should start and end with alphanumeric characters for consistency and to avoid edge cases in URL processing.
    75→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    76→- Hyphens at the beginning of the slug are removed
    77→- Hyphens at the end of the slug are removed
    78→- Internal hyphens remain unchanged
    79→- Example: "-hello-world-" → "hello-world"
    80→
    81→### REQ-006: Function Interface
    82→**Priority**: Must Have
    83→**Actor**: Developer
    84→**Description**: The utility must be exposed as a function named `slugify` that accepts a single text parameter and returns a string.
    85→**Rationale**: Clear, standard function naming and interface enables easy discovery and usage by developers.
    86→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    87→- Function is named `slugify`
    88→- Function accepts one parameter: a string to be converted
    89→- Function returns a string containing the slugified result
    90→- Function is exported from the utils module for reuse
    91→
    92→## User Stories
    93→
    94→### STORY-001: Developer Uses Slugify for Title Conversion
    95→**As a** developer implementing a feature
    96→**I want** to convert user-provided titles into URL-safe slugs
    97→**So that** I can generate consistent, readable URLs without manual string manipulation
    98→
    99→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   100→- GIVEN a user title "Hello, World!"
   101→- WHEN I call `slugify("Hello, World!")`
   102→- THEN I receive "hello-world"
   103→
   104→### STORY-002: Developer Handles Text with Multiple Spaces
   105→**As a** developer
   106→**I want** the slugify function to normalize irregular spacing
   107→**So that** inconsistent user input produces clean, uniform slugs
   108→
   109→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   110→- GIVEN text with multiple spaces "Foo  Bar"
   111→- WHEN I call `slugify("Foo  Bar")`
   112→- THEN I receive "foo-bar"
   113→
   114→### STORY-003: Developer Converts Underscored Text
   115→**As a** developer
   116→**I want** underscores to be converted to hyphens
   117→**So that** slugs follow URL conventions regardless of input format
   118→
   119→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   120→- GIVEN text with underscores "Foo__Bar"
   121→- WHEN I call `slugify("Foo__Bar")`
   122→- THEN I receive "foo-bar"
   123→
   124→### STORY-004: Developer Normalizes Hyphenated Text
   125→**As a** developer
   126→**I want** excessive hyphens to be collapsed
   127→**So that** slugs remain concise and readable
   128→
   129→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   130→- GIVEN text with repeated hyphens "a---b"
   131→- WHEN I call `slugify("a---b")`
   132→- THEN I receive "a-b"
   133→
   134→## Test Cases
   135→
   136→### TC-001: Basic Text with Punctuation
   137→- **Input**: "Hello, World!"
   138→- **Expected Output**: "hello-world"
   139→- **Validates**: REQ-001, REQ-002, REQ-003
   140→
   141→### TC-002: Multiple Spaces
   142→- **Input**: "Foo  Bar"
   143→- **Expected Output**: "foo-bar"
   144→- **Validates**: REQ-002, REQ-004
   145→
   146→### TC-003: Multiple Underscores
   147→- **Input**: "Foo__Bar"
   148→- **Expected Output**: "foo-bar"
   149→- **Validates**: REQ-002, REQ-004
   150→
   151→### TC-004: Repeated Hyphens
   152→- **Input**: "a---b"
   153→- **Expected Output**: "a-b"
   154→- **Validates**: REQ-004
   155→
   156→### TC-005: Leading and Trailing Hyphens
   157→- **Input**: "-hello-world-"
   158→- **Expected Output**: "hello-world"
   159→- **Validates**: REQ-005
   160→
   161→### TC-006: Mixed Case
   162→- **Input**: "HeLLo WoRLd"
   163→- **Expected Output**: "hello-world"
   164→- **Validates**: REQ-001, REQ-002
   165→
   166→### TC-007: Alphanumeric with Special Characters
   167→- **Input**: "Test123!@#456"
   168→- **Expected Output**: "test123456"
   169→- **Validates**: REQ-001, REQ-003
   170→
   171→### TC-008: Empty String
   172→- **Input**: ""
   173→- **Expected Output**: ""
   174→- **Validates**: All requirements (edge case)
   175→
   176→### TC-009: Only Special Characters
   177→- **Input**: "!@#$%"
   178→- **Expected Output**: ""
   179→- **Validates**: REQ-003, REQ-005 (edge case)
   180→
   181→### TC-010: Complex Real-World Example
   182→- **Input**: "  Hello,  World!__Test---123  "
   183→- **Expected Output**: "hello-world-test-123"
   184→- **Validates**: All requirements combined
   185→
   186→## Non-Functional Requirements
   187→
   188→### NFR-001: Performance
   189→**Category**: Performance
   190→**Description**: The slugify function must execute efficiently for typical input strings (up to 1000 characters).
   191→**Rationale**: String utilities are often called frequently and should not introduce performance bottlenecks.
   192→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   193→- Function completes in under 10ms for strings up to 1000 characters
   194→- No memory leaks or excessive allocations
   195→
   196→### NFR-002: Reliability
   197→**Category**: Reliability
   198→**Description**: The function must handle all string inputs without errors, including edge cases like empty strings, Unicode characters, and very long strings.
   199→**Rationale**: Defensive programming prevents runtime errors in production.
   200→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   201→- Function never throws exceptions for any string input
   202→- Function handles null/undefined gracefully (if applicable to language)
   203→- Function handles Unicode characters appropriately (either preserve or remove consistently)
   204→
   205→### NFR-003: Maintainability
   206→**Category**: Maintainability
   207→**Description**: The implementation must be clear, well-documented, and testable.
   208→**Rationale**: Utility functions should be easy to understand and modify as requirements evolve.
   209→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   210→- Function includes inline comments explaining transformation logic
   211→- Function is covered by unit tests
   212→- Function logic is broken into clear, sequential steps
   213→
   214→## Success Metrics
   215→
   216→- **Functional Completeness**: All test cases (TC-001 through TC-010) pass
   217→- **Test Coverage**: 100% code coverage for the slugify function
   218→- **Usage Adoption**: Function is used in at least one feature requiring slug generation
   219→
   220→## Dependencies
   221→
   222→None identified. This is a standalone utility function.
   223→
   224→## Constraints
   225→
   226→- Must be implemented in TypeScript (per project tech stack)
   227→- Must be added to the existing `src/utils.ts` module
   228→- Must follow existing project code patterns
   229→
   230→## Out of Scope
   231→
   232→- Internationalization (Unicode transliteration, e.g., converting "café" to "cafe")
   233→- Custom separator characters (only hyphens are supported)
   234→- Maximum length truncation
   235→- Uniqueness guarantees (responsibility of caller)
   236→- Slug validation or parsing (inverse operation)
   237→
   238→## AFK Mode Decisions
   239→
   240→This requirements document was generated in AFK (autonomous) mode. The following decisions were made automatically:
   241→
   242→### Decision 1: No PRD Association
   243→**Point**: PRD selection

     4→created: 2026-07-29

     9→---
    10→
    11→# Technical Design: Slugify String Utility
    12→
    13→## Overview
    14→
    15→This design describes the implementation of a `slugify` utility function that transforms arbitrary strings into URL-safe, normalized slug formats. The function will be added to the existing `src/utils.ts` module following established project patterns.
    16→
    17→## Architecture
    18→
    19→### System Context
    20→
    21→```mermaid
    22→flowchart LR
    23→    subgraph Application
    24→        A[src/index.ts] --> B[src/utils.ts]
    25→        C[Future Features] --> B
    26→    end
    27→    B --> D[slugify function]
    28→```
    29→
    30→The `slugify` function is a pure utility with no external dependencies. It integrates into the existing utils module and can be consumed by any module requiring slug generation.
    31→
    32→### Component Design
    33→
    34→```mermaid
    35→flowchart TD
    36→    Input[Input String] --> Step1[1. Lowercase Conversion]
    37→    Step1 --> Step2[2. Whitespace/Underscore Replacement]
    38→    Step2 --> Step3[3. Character Filtering]
    39→    Step3 --> Step4[4. Hyphen Collapsing]
    40→    Step4 --> Step5[5. Hyphen Trimming]
    41→    Step5 --> Output[Output Slug]
    42→```
    43→
    44→The function implements a five-step transformation pipeline:
    45→
    46→| Step | Operation | Implementation |
    47→|------|-----------|----------------|
    48→| 1 | Lowercase conversion | `String.prototype.toLowerCase()` |
    49→| 2 | Whitespace/underscore replacement | Regex: `/[\s_]+/g` -> `-` |
    50→| 3 | Character filtering | Regex: `/[^a-z0-9-]/g` -> `` |
    51→| 4 | Hyphen collapsing | Regex: `/-+/g` -> `-` |
    52→| 5 | Hyphen trimming | Regex: `/^-+\|-+$/g` -> `` |
    53→
    54→### Data Flow
    55→
    56→```mermaid
    57→sequenceDiagram
    58→    participant Caller
    59→    participant slugify
    60→
    61→    Caller->>slugify: "Hello, World!"
    62→    Note over slugify: toLowerCase()
    63→    Note over slugify: "hello, world!"
    64→    Note over slugify: replace /[\s_]+/g
    65→    Note over slugify: "hello,-world!"
    66→    Note over slugify: replace /[^a-z0-9-]/g
    67→    Note over slugify: "hello-world"
    68→    Note over slugify: replace /-+/g
    69→    Note over slugify: "hello-world"
    70→    Note over slugify: trim hyphens
    71→    slugify-->>Caller: "hello-world"
    72→```
    73→
    74→## Technical Specification
    75→
    76→### Function Interface
    77→
    78→```typescript
    79→/**
    80→ * Convert a string to a URL-safe slug.
    81→ *
    82→ * Transforms input by:
    83→ * 1. Converting to lowercase
    84→ * 2. Replacing spaces and underscores with hyphens
    85→ * 3. Removing non-alphanumeric characters (except hyphens)
    86→ * 4. Collapsing multiple consecutive hyphens
    87→ * 5. Trimming leading and trailing hyphens
    88→ *
    89→ * @param text - The string to slugify
    90→ * @returns A URL-safe slug string
    91→ *
    92→ * @example
    93→ * slugify("Hello, World!") // "hello-world"
    94→ * slugify("Foo  Bar")      // "foo-bar"
    95→ * slugify("a---b")         // "a-b"
    96→ */
    97→export function slugify(text: string): string;
    98→```
    99→
   100→### Implementation Approach
   101→
   102→The implementation uses a chain of string transformations:
   103→
   104→```typescript
   105→export function slugify(text: string): string {
   106→  return text
   107→    .toLowerCase()                    // REQ-001: Case normalization
   108→    .replace(/[\s_]+/g, '-')          // REQ-002: Whitespace/underscore -> hyphen
   109→    .replace(/[^a-z0-9-]/g, '')       // REQ-003: Remove invalid characters
   110→    .replace(/-+/g, '-')              // REQ-004: Collapse multiple hyphens
   111→    .replace(/^-+|-+$/g, '');         // REQ-005: Trim leading/trailing hyphens
   112→}
   113→```
   114→
   115→### Edge Case Handling
   116→
   117→| Input | Output | Rationale |
   118→|-------|--------|-----------|
   119→| Empty string `""` | `""` | Pass-through, no transformation needed |
   120→| Only special chars `"!@#$%"` | `""` | All chars filtered, hyphens trimmed |
   121→| Only whitespace `"   "` | `""` | Converted to hyphens, then trimmed |
   122→| Unicode chars `"cafe"` | `"cafe"` | ASCII letters preserved |
   123→| Unicode chars `"caf?"` | `"caf"` | Non-ASCII removed per REQ-003 |
   124→
   125→### Type Safety
   126→
   127→TypeScript enforces the string input type at compile time. Runtime null/undefined checks are unnecessary as:
   128→1. TypeScript strict mode prevents null/undefined assignment to string
   129→2. The function operates on primitive string operations that handle empty strings gracefully
   130→
   131→## Integration Points
   132→
   133→### Module Integration
   134→
   135→| Integration | Source | Target | Type |
   136→|-------------|--------|--------|------|
   137→| Export | `src/utils.ts` | Consumers | Named export |
   138→| Import | Consumer modules | `src/utils.ts` | ESM import |
   139→
   140→Example usage:
   141→```typescript
   142→import { slugify } from "./utils";
   143→
   144→const slug = slugify("Hello, World!"); // "hello-world"
   145→```
   146→
   147→## Testing Strategy
   148→
   149→### Test Categories
   150→
   151→| Category | Description | Coverage |
   152→|----------|-------------|----------|
   153→| Basic transformation | Standard inputs with punctuation, spaces | TC-001 |
   154→| Whitespace handling | Multiple spaces, tabs | TC-002 |
   155→| Underscore handling | Single and multiple underscores | TC-003 |
   156→| Hyphen handling | Multiple hyphens, leading/trailing | TC-004, TC-005 |
   157→| Case normalization | Mixed case inputs | TC-006 |
   158→| Character filtering | Special characters, symbols | TC-007 |
   159→| Edge cases | Empty string, only special chars | TC-008, TC-009 |
   160→| Complex inputs | Combined transformations | TC-010 |
   161→
   162→### Test Implementation
   163→
   164→Tests will be added to `src/utils.test.ts` following the existing pattern:
   165→
   166→```typescript
   167→describe("slugify", () => {
   168→  test("converts text with punctuation to slug", () => {
   169→    expect(slugify("Hello, World!")).toBe("hello-world");
   170→  });
   171→
   172→  test("collapses multiple spaces", () => {
   173→    expect(slugify("Foo  Bar")).toBe("foo-bar");
   174→  });
   175→
   176→  // ... additional test cases
   177→});
   178→```
   179→
   180→### Coverage Requirements
   181→
   182→- All 10 test cases from requirements must pass
   183→- Each requirement (REQ-001 through REQ-006) must have at least one test
   184→- Edge cases (empty string, only special chars) must be covered
   185→
   186→## Performance Considerations
   187→
   188→### Complexity Analysis
   189→
   190→| Operation | Complexity | Notes |
   191→|-----------|------------|-------|
   192→| toLowerCase | O(n) | Single pass |
   193→| Each regex replace | O(n) | Single pass per regex |
   194→| Total | O(n) | Linear in input length |
   195→
   196→### Benchmarks
   197→
   198→For typical inputs (< 1000 characters), expected execution time is < 1ms. The regex engine is highly optimized for these simple patterns.
   199→
   200→### Memory
   201→
   202→- No intermediate allocations beyond string results
   203→- Chained method calls create temporary strings (expected JavaScript behavior)
   204→- No memory leaks possible (pure function, no retained references)
   205→
   206→## Error Handling
   207→
   208→The function is designed to never throw exceptions:
   209→
   210→| Scenario | Behavior |
   211→|----------|----------|
   212→| Empty string | Returns empty string |
   213→| Null/undefined | TypeScript prevents; if bypassed, `.toLowerCase()` would throw |
   214→| Very long string | Processes linearly; JavaScript string limit is ~512MB |
   215→
   216→For defensive runtime handling (if needed for JavaScript consumers), a guard could be added:
   217→```typescript
   218→if (typeof text !== 'string') return '';
   219→```
   220→
   221→This is **not recommended** for the initial implementation as TypeScript provides compile-time guarantees.
   222→
   223→## Implementation Plan
   224→
   225→### Task Breakdown
   226→
   227→| Task | Description | Estimate |
   228→|------|-------------|----------|
   229→| T1 | Implement `slugify` function in `src/utils.ts` | 10 min |
   230→| T2 | Add test cases to `src/utils.test.ts` | 15 min |
   231→
